summary:
ASTRA CARE is an interactive web prototype built for the ORBITCARE – Health Monitoring Beyond Earth challenge to support crew wellbeing during long-duration space missions. We developed a browser-based health intelligence system where astronauts can log daily vital signs, sleep hours, physical symptoms, and mental wellbeing indicators, alongside an Action Guidance tool and a 150-day mission simulator.
The project addresses the challenge by replacing generic medical averages with an individualized tracking approach. Using a crew member's first five check-ins as a personal baseline, the system identifies repeated shifts across three or more entries and explains why those patterns deserve attention, while keeping synthetic telemetry strictly separate from real NASA research sources.
This solution is important because communication delays during deep-space travel make real-time Earth support difficult. Giving astronauts clear, understandable feedback on gradual physical and psychological changes empowers them to spot early warning signs and hold better-informed reviews with mission medical officers.
details: ASTRA CARE works as a daily health companion for astronauts during long missions. Each day, a crew member enters basic physical numbers—such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, and sleep hours—along with any physical symptoms. They also rate their mood, stress, energy, focus, and connection with the crew. Instead of comparing everyone to a standard medical chart, the system uses a person's first five check-ins to learn their normal personal baseline. When a measurement changes across three or more check-ins in a row, the system highlights the pattern and explains why it matters. Users can also test how the system reacts over time using a built-in 150-day mission simulator. Benefits and Intended Impact In space, a single unusual reading does not always mean a serious problem, which makes it hard to know when to worry. By focusing on repeated patterns, ASTRA CARE helps astronauts notice gradual changes in their sleep, stress, or physical health before they become bigger risks. It also includes an Action Guidance feature that suggests practical next steps and lets crew members download clean reports to share with flight surgeons. Our main goal is to support crew independence and make health conversations between astronauts and medical teams faster, clearer, and more accurate during deep-space travel. Tools and Technologies Used We built the entire web application using core front-end languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. All user check-ins are saved directly inside the web browser's local storage so the app works smoothly without an active internet connection. We also wrote custom JavaScript logic to calculate baselines, detect repeated trends, power the interactive mission simulation, and generate downloadable JSON and CSV files. Creativity and Key Factors Considered • Clear Logic Instead of Guessing: Many health tools act like a "black box" and give warnings without explaining why. We designed ASTRA CARE to show the exact numbers and rules behind every observation so users can trust the results. • Honesty About Data and Safety: Our team made sure to keep fictional simulator numbers completely separate from real spaceflight research, and we added clear reminders that the app is an educational tool rather than a medical device. • Designed for Space Conditions: Because astronauts often work in low-light cabins and face communication delays with Earth, we chose a dark, easy-to-read interface that runs fully offline with zero server delays.
